source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 20 (book page 273); the book prints no answers for Exercise 9.2; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
Each term is a double-angle form met earlier in this exercise.
Plan: write all three terms as \(2\tan^{-1}(\ldots)\) (Question 12, Question 14 (i) and the book's \(2\tan^{-1} x\) formula), divide by 2, join with formula (v), and take \(\tan\).
steps:
Given: \(\sin^{-1}\frac{2p}{1 + p^2} + \cos^{-1}\frac{1 - q^2}{1 + q^2} = \tan^{-1}\frac{2y}{1 - y^2}\).
To show: \(y = \frac{p + q}{1 - pq}\).
Method: Recognise the three double-angle forms; they turn the equation into one between \(\tan^{-1} p\), \(\tan^{-1} q\) and \(\tan^{-1} y\). As the book does, we take the values for which these results hold: \(-1 \le p \le 1\), \(q \ge 0\), \(-1 < y < 1\) and \(pq < 1\).

Replace each term
\[\sin^{-1}\dfrac{2p}{1 + p^2} = 2\tan^{-1} p\]
\[\cos^{-1}\dfrac{1 - q^2}{1 + q^2} = 2\tan^{-1} q\]
\[\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2y}{1 - y^2} = 2\tan^{-1} y\]
Why: Question 12 (for \(-1 \le p \le 1\)), Question 14 (i) (for \(q \ge 0\)), and the book's result \(2\tan^{-1} x = \tan^{-1}\frac{2x}{1 - x^2}\) from Section 9.2 (for \(-1 < y < 1\)).

Substitute and divide by 2
\[2\tan^{-1} p + 2\tan^{-1} q = 2\tan^{-1} y\]
\[\tan^{-1} p + \tan^{-1} q = \tan^{-1} y\]
Why: Every term has the factor 2.

Join with formula (v)
\[\tan^{-1}\dfrac{p + q}{1 - pq} = \tan^{-1} y\]
Why: Formula (v) with \(pq < 1\).

Take \(\tan\) of both sides
\[y = \dfrac{p + q}{1 - pq}\]
Why: \(\tan(\tan^{-1} u) = u\) for every real \(u\).

Check
\[p = 0.3,\ q = 0.4:\ y = \dfrac{0.7}{0.88} \approx 0.7955\]
\[\sin^{-1}\dfrac{0.6}{1.09} \approx 0.5829\]
\[\cos^{-1}\dfrac{0.84}{1.16} \approx 0.7610\]
\[\text{sum} \approx 0.5829 + 0.7610\]
\[= 1.3439\]
\[\tan^{-1}\dfrac{2y}{1 - y^2} \approx \tan^{-1} 4.3319 \approx 1.3439\]
Why: Both sides of the given equation agree for this \(y\).
